answer: A seating board keeps a locked vault of reference pigment tiles and publishes an atlas of each tile's measured reflectance curve. An applicant may rent only one tile, must reproduce that curve from a fresh mix under a witnessed spectrophotometer, and posts the mix formula on-chain. A failed match, or a second claim on the same tile, burns the deposit and returns the tile to the board. Key farms can mint identities cheaply, but they cannot occupy two atlas tiles or fake a vault match, so sybil swarms stall at the vault door.
